ne631e1c89a8.s: Which of the following hazard–region associations in India is NOT correct?
o: Drought – Rajasthan and the Deccan interior
ne631e1c89a8.x: Landslides are associated with the Himalaya and Western Ghats, not the Thar Desert; the other pairs are correct.

ndisaster-management-31-11.s: Lahaul-Spiti and Kinnaur, known avalanche-prone areas, are in:
ndisaster-management-31-11.x: Lahaul-Spiti and Kinnaur are avalanche-prone areas of Himachal Pradesh, not Uttarakhand (whose avalanche zones are in Garhwal and Kumaon).

ndisaster-management-4-2.x: Tsunami is Japanese for 'harbour wave'; it is not a tidal wave.

nf81c7e4cc48.s: Heatwaves and lightning were added to India's notified-disaster list for 2026-31 on the recommendation of the:
nf81c7e4cc48.x: The addition (12 to 14 notified disasters) was made on the Sixteenth Finance Commission's recommendation, not the Fifteenth.

nf6ceb706428.s: Which of the following disaster–year pairs is NOT correctly matched?
nf6ceb706428.x: The Bhuj earthquake struck in 2001, not 2004; Latur was 1993, the Odisha super cyclone 1999 and the Indian Ocean tsunami 2004.

n078ab5b2da6.s: Under the revised coastline figures (2023-24), Andhra Pradesh's coastline ranks:
n078ab5b2da6.x: Andhra Pradesh (1,053.07 km) is third; Gujarat is first and Tamil Nadu second.

ndisaster-management-17-17.s: The nodal ministry for urban floods in India is the Ministry of:
ndisaster-management-17-17.x: Urban floods come under Housing and Urban Affairs; the Environment Ministry handles forest fires.

nbb4e748cdbc.s: Which of the following was an emphasis of the 2009 National Policy on Disaster Management?
o: Promoting preparedness only after a disaster occurs
nbb4e748cdbc.x: The 2009 policy emphasised prevention, mitigation, community participation and mainstreaming DRR; reliance on post-disaster relief runs against it.

nf7fc2111904.s: The National Centre for Disaster Management at IIPA was set up in:
nf7fc2111904.x: The NCDM was set up in 1995, before the DM Act (2005), the National Policy (2009) and the Sendai Framework (2015).

ndisaster-management-20-16.s: The High Powered Committee on Disaster Management (1999) grouped disasters into how many broad categories?
ndisaster-management-20-16.x: The High Powered Committee, set up in 1999 under J. C. Pant, classified disasters into five broad categories.

n04a4f26dd47.s: Which Central fund tops up the State Disaster Response Fund during severe calamities?
n04a4f26dd47.x: The National Disaster Response Fund supplements the SDRF in severe calamities; the mitigation funds are for long-term risk reduction.

n014c0299fd8.s: The National Disaster Response Force draws its personnel from the:
n014c0299fd8.x: The NDRF is a specialist force drawn from central paramilitary forces; the SDRF draws on State Police, Home Guards, Fire Services and Civil Defence.

ndisaster-management-21-5.s: Which of the following is a notified disaster for SDRF assistance?
ndisaster-management-21-5.x: Frost and cold wave are on the notified list; no man-made calamity is notified for SDRF help.

ndisaster-management-2-27.s: The disaster management cycle is continuous because:
o: Lessons from recovery lead to better prevention
ndisaster-management-2-27.x: The cycle is continuous since lessons from recovery feed into better prevention.

ndisaster-management-26-4.s: Storm surge modelling with GIS is used mainly for which hazard?
ndisaster-management-26-4.x: GIS models storm surges for cyclones; for floods it maps inundation and for droughts it supports NADAMS.

n84713938496.s: Under UNCLOS, full sovereignty subject to innocent passage applies in the:
n84713938496.x: The territorial sea (12 nm) gives full sovereignty subject to innocent passage; the high seas carry freedom of navigation.

nf726e816d2e.s: The UN Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) was adopted in:
nf726e816d2e.x: UNCLOS was adopted in 1982 and came into force in 1994; it set up the International Seabed Authority.

n32d65d9d897.s: How many offshore mineral blocks were in the first tranche auctioned under a composite licence (November 2024)?
n32d65d9d897.x: The first tranche, auctioned on 28 November 2024 under the OAMDR Act, had 13 offshore blocks.

n9acfc0e754c.s: Which of the following favours the development of major fishing grounds?
o: Highly arid interiors with no coastal access
Mixing of warm and cold currents
n9acfc0e754c.x: Wide shallow shelves, mixing of warm and cold currents, upwelling and indented coasts favour fishing grounds.

n75dd2990dff.s: Inland fisheries contribute about what share of India's fish production?
n75dd2990dff.x: Inland fisheries contribute more than 75% of India's fish production.

n52ac6a3f1b0.s: Under the EEZ Rules, 2025, the Access Pass for vessels of 24 m or more is issued:
o: Through ReALCraft on payment of a fee
n52ac6a3f1b0.x: The Access Pass, mandatory for mechanised and motorised vessels of at least 24 m, is issued through ReALCraft at zero fee; traditional crafts are exempt.

new.s: The Bhola cyclone of 1970 struck present-day:
new.x: The 1970 Bhola cyclone hit East Pakistan, now Bangladesh.

new.s: The Crete tsunami of 365 CE is associated with which country?
new.x: The Crete tsunami (365 CE) is listed among the world's worst disasters, in Greece.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (disaster – country) is INCORRECTLY matched?
new.x: The Crete tsunami (365 CE) was in Greece; the Yellow River flood (1931) was in China and the Tohoku tsunami (2011) in Japan.

new.s: The gas that leaked in the Bhopal disaster of December 1984 was:
new.x: The Union Carbide pesticide plant at Bhopal leaked methyl isocyanate (MIC) on 2–3 December 1984.

new.s: The Chernobyl nuclear disaster occurred in:
new.x: Chernobyl (Pripyat, Ukraine, then USSR) was the reactor No. 4 explosion of 26 April 1986; Bhopal was 1984 and Fukushima 2011.

new.s: The Fukushima Daiichi nuclear disaster (11 March 2011) was triggered by:
new.x: A Mw 9.0 earthquake and the tsunami it caused led to meltdowns and radiation release at Fukushima Daiichi.

new.s: The Latur (Killari) earthquake of 30 September 1993 struck which State?
new.x: The Latur (Killari) earthquake of 1993 struck Maharashtra; the Bhuj earthquake of 2001 struck Gujarat.

new.s: The Bhuj earthquake of 26 January 2001 struck:
new.x: The Bhuj earthquake of 2001 hit Kutch in Gujarat; Killari was the 1993 Latur quake and Paradip the 1999 super cyclone.

new.s: The Mumbai flood of 26 July 2005 followed about how much rain in 24 hours?
new.x: Mumbai received 944 mm in 24 hours on 26 July 2005, and its drainage failed.

new.s: The Chennai flood of December 2015 was aggravated mainly by:
new.x: Chennai's 2015 flood came from extreme rain worsened by wetland destruction; the Kosi flood was an embankment breach and Kerala 2018 involved dam releases.

new.s: The Kerala floods of August 2018 were caused by heavy rain and:
new.x: The 2018 Kerala floods resulted from heavy rain and dam releases.

new.s: In India, flood control is a:
new.x: Flood control is a State subject; the Centre helps through the Flood Management and Border Areas Programme (FMBAP).

new.s: The Centre assists States in flood control through:
new.x: The Centre supports States' flood control through FMBAP; PMFBY is crop insurance and HSDPR concerns CBRN medical centres.

new.s: How many of India's 36 States/UTs are disaster-prone?
new.x: 27 of India's 36 States/UTs are disaster-prone.

new.s: Earthquakes, tsunamis, landslides and avalanches are classified as ____ disasters.
new.x: Earthquakes, tsunamis, landslides and avalanches are geological; droughts and heatwaves are climatological.

new.s: Droughts, heatwaves and cold waves are classified as:
new.x: Droughts, heatwaves and cold waves are climatological; floods and cloudbursts are hydrological.

new.s: According to GRID 2025, India recorded about how many disaster displacements in 2024?
new.x: India had 5.4 million disaster displacements in 2024, the highest in 12 years; 32.3 million is its total for 2015–2024.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about tsunami threats to India:
1. The Sunda-Andaman subduction zone threatens the east.
2. The Makran zone threatens the west coast.
3. Andaman & Nicobar is in the moderate risk zone.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; Andaman & Nicobar is in the very high risk zone, not moderate.

new.s: Drought in which water demand exceeds supply and shortages hit livelihoods and markets is:
new.x: Socio-economic drought arises when demand exceeds supply and shortages hit livelihoods and markets; it has the longest time lag.

new.s: As per IMD, a rainfall deficiency of 26–50% of the long-period average is a:
new.x: IMD treats a 26–50% deficiency as moderate drought and over 50% as severe drought.

new.s: The Leh cloudburst in Ladakh occurred in:
new.x: The Leh cloudburst was in 2010; Kedarnath was 2013 and the Chamoli glacier burst 2021.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about storm surges?
o: They are pushed by cyclone winds and low pressure
The west coast gets far more cyclones than the east
A high tide raises their baseline
new.x: The east coast, not the west, gets far more cyclones; the other statements are correct.

new.s: Flood insurance and flood-plain zoning are examples of:
new.x: Flood insurance, flood-plain zoning and flood-proofing are non-structural; dams and channel improvement are structural.

new.s: The National Institute of Disaster Management is provided for under which Section of the DM Act, 2005?
new.x: Section 42 provides for NIDM; s.44 is the NDRF force, s.46 the NDRF fund and s.25 the DDMA.

new.s: The National Disaster Response Force is constituted under which Section of the DM Act, 2005?
new.x: The NDRF force is under s.44; the National Disaster Response Fund is under s.46.

new.s: The National Executive Committee is constituted under which Section of the DM Act, 2005?
new.x: s.8 creates the NEC; s.3 the NDMA, s.14 the SDMA and s.25 the DDMA.

new.s: The National Disaster Mitigation Fund is provided under which Section of the DM Act, 2005?
new.x: s.47 provides for the mitigation fund; s.46 is the National Disaster Response Fund and s.48 the SDRF.

new.s: The National Disaster Response Force was raised in:
new.x: The NDRF was raised in 2006 under s.44; 2005 is the year of the DM Act.

new.s: The NDRF observes its Raising Day on:
new.x: NDRF Raising Day is 19 January; 27 September 2006 is NDMA's constitution and 23 December 2005 the Act's assent.

new.s: Each NDRF battalion has how many search-and-rescue teams?
new.x: Each NDRF battalion has 18 search-and-rescue teams; the force has 16 battalions.

new.s: The Southern Campus of the National Institute of Disaster Management is at:
new.x: NIDM's Southern Campus is at Kondapalli near Vijayawada, not Visakhapatnam.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (institution – location) is INCORRECTLY matched?
new.x: The Central Water Commission is in New Delhi, not Hyderabad; the other pairs are correct.

new.s: The Centre for Disaster Management that trains civil servants is located at:
new.x: The Centre for Disaster Management at LBSNAA, Mussoorie trains civil servants.

new.s: The first India Disaster Management Congress (November 2006) was held in:
new.x: NIDM organised the first India Disaster Management Congress in New Delhi in November 2006.

new.s: The Disaster Management Institute set up in 1987 after the gas tragedy is at:
new.x: The Disaster Management Institute, Bhopal was set up in 1987 after the Bhopal gas tragedy.

new.s: Disaster management was shifted from the Ministry of Agriculture to the Ministry of Home Affairs in:
new.x: The subject moved from Agriculture to Home Affairs in 2002, after the 2001 Gujarat earthquake.

new.s: The Hyogo Framework for Action covered the period:
new.x: The Hyogo Framework (adopted at Kobe, January 2005) ran 2005–2015 and was replaced by the Sendai Framework (2015–2030).

new.s: India launched the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure (CDRI) in 2019 at the:
o: UN Climate Action Summit, New York
new.x: CDRI was launched by India at the UN Climate Action Summit in New York in 2019; its secretariat is in New Delhi.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Sendai Framework:
1. It covers the period 2015–2030.
2. It sets 7 global targets.
3. It has five priorities for action.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; the Sendai Framework has four priorities for action, not five.

new.s: The National Disaster Management Plan 2016 sets short, medium and long time frames of:
new.x: NDMP 2016 uses short (5-year), medium (10-year) and long (15-year) time frames.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a safe action during a cyclone?
new.x: During a cyclone one should never stand under trees or go to sea; moving to a shelter or safe building is advised.

new.s: Indoors during an earthquake, the safest action is to:
o: Drop, cover and hold under a strong table
new.x: Indoors, 'Drop! Cover! Hold' under a strong table, away from windows, balconies and stairs, is safest.

new.s: IMD's Damini app gives warnings about:
new.x: IMD's Damini app is for lightning; tsunamis are with INCOIS, landslides with GSI and river floods with CWC.

new.s: India's earthquake early-warning pilot in Uttarakhand is run by:
new.x: IIT Roorkee runs the earthquake early-warning pilot in Uttarakhand; the National Centre for Seismology (MoES) is the earthquake agency.

new.s: Cyclone Hudhud (October 2014) made landfall at:
new.x: Hudhud struck Visakhapatnam in 2014; Titli came near Palasa (2018) and Michaung near Bapatla (2023).

new.s: Which of the following pairs (cyclone – landfall) is correctly matched?
new.x: Titli (2018) made landfall near Palasa in Srikakulam; Hudhud hit Visakhapatnam and Michaung came near Bapatla.

new.s: Up to what share of its SDRF may a State spend on state-specific disasters?
new.x: Up to 10% (not 25%) of the SDRF may go to state-specific disasters.

new.s: The National Platform for Disaster Risk Reduction (NPDRR) is headed by the:
new.x: NPDRR, a multi-stakeholder DRR platform, is headed by the Union Home Minister.

new.s: The Bhopal gas tragedy (2–3 December 1984) is an example of a:
new.x: The Bhopal gas tragedy, a methyl isocyanate leak, was a man-made disaster.

new.s: Disaster risk falls with an increase in:
new.x: Risk rises with hazard, exposure and vulnerability and falls with coping capacity.

new.s: INSAT-3D/3DR satellites are used in disaster management mainly to:
new.x: INSAT-3D/3DR are used to track cyclones.

new.s: Under UNCLOS, the contiguous zone extends up to how far from the baseline?
new.x: The contiguous zone reaches 24 nm; the territorial sea is 12 nm and the EEZ 200 nm.

new.s: A coastal state's continental shelf can extend up to:
new.x: The continental shelf (seabed and subsoil) can extend up to 350 nm.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about UNCLOS maritime zones?
o: Contiguous zone – Customs and immigration laws
new.x: In the EEZ the coastal state has only sovereign rights over resources; full sovereignty applies in the 12 nm territorial sea.

new.s: The Grand Banks fishing ground lies off:
new.x: The Grand Banks lie off Newfoundland in the NW Atlantic, where the Gulf Stream meets the Labrador Current.

new.s: Dogger Bank, a shallow sandbank fishing ground, lies in the:
new.x: Dogger Bank is a shallow sandbank in the North Sea, about 100 km off eastern England.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about pearl production:
1. Japan is the classic largest producer of cultured Akoya pearls.
2. By volume, China now leads.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Both are correct: Japan is the classic producer of cultured Akoya pearls, while China now leads by volume.

new.s: Polymetallic nodules of the Central Indian Ocean Basin mainly carry:
new.x: Polymetallic nodules carry nickel, copper, cobalt and manganese; monazite and ilmenite are beach placers and gas hydrates are methane ice.

new.s: India's third ISA contract (15 September 2025), for polymetallic sulphides, covers the:
o: Central and South West Indian Ridge
new.x: Contract 3 (2025) is for sulphides on the Carlsberg Ridge; Contract 2 (2016) covered the Central and South West Indian Ridge.

new.s: Samudrayaan's submersible Matsya 6000 is designed to carry how many crew to 6,000 m?
new.x: Matsya 6000 is an indigenous submersible for 3 crew to 6,000 m.

new.s: The Deep Ocean Mission, approved in June 2021 for 5 years, has an outlay of about:
new.x: The Deep Ocean Mission (MoES) was approved with ₹4,077 crore for 5 years.

new.s: Monazite, found in beach placers, is an ore of:
new.x: Monazite yields thorium; ilmenite yields titanium.

new.s: Which of the following is an oil and gas basin of India?
new.x: Mumbai High is an oil and gas basin; Chavara, Manavalakurichi and Chatrapur are beach placer sites.

new.s: In India's territorial waters (0–12 nm), fisheries are a:
new.x: Fisheries within 0–12 nm are a State subject; 12–200 nm comes under the Centre.

new.s: Under PMMSY, the subsidy for women, SC and ST beneficiaries is:
new.x: PMMSY gives 40% subsidy to general beneficiaries and 60% to women, SC and ST.

new.s: The SAGAR vision was articulated by the Prime Minister in 2015 in:
new.x: SAGAR ('Security and Growth for All in the Region') was articulated in Mauritius in 2015.

new.s: Andhra Pradesh accounts for about what share of India's fish production?
new.x: Andhra Pradesh produces about 30% of India's fish and 31% of its shrimp exports.

new.s: Andhra Pradesh's offshore oil and gas lie mainly in the:
new.x: AP's oil and gas are in the Krishna-Godavari (KG) basin.
